params.name: min_support
params.why: 1% of training clients = 330 people: the smallest group worth a targeted call list.

params.name: min_confidence
params.why: Rules must hold at least 30% of the time — ~2.7× the 11.27% base rate for y=yes.

params.name: min_lift
params.why: Reporting filter: a rule must lift the subscription rate by at least 20% over chance.

params.name: min_improvement
params.why: Redundancy filter (Bayardo, Agrawal & Gunopulos 1999): adding an item must raise confidence by ≥ 2 points over every simpler rule, otherwise the longer rule is just the shorter one restated.

params.name: max_len
params.why: Itemsets up to 4 items (the L1–L4 progression); longer rules have tiny coverage and are hard to act on.

params.name: binning
params.why: Rules need discrete items. Terciles keep each macro bin around a third of clients where ties allow.

params.name: mining data
params.why: So rules can be re-checked on held-out clients, like every other model.
